_comment: Defaults every Herald install shares. The user's own settings live in $HERALD_HOME/config.json and are merged over this file, so a default improved in a Herald update reaches installs that never touched it. Nothing personal belongs here.
name: herald

agent.name: Herald
agent._name_comment: What this install's agent calls itself. Set at setup; the personal constitution in ledger/identity/constitution.md is where it is stated to the agent.

engines._comment: Choose claude, codex, or both during setup. enabled lists the providers you use (null keeps both available for existing installs). default_engine is your choice for cycles, terminal sessions and new Telegram topics; null requires a choice. Model and effort null use the selected CLI defaults. No provider is preferred and failures never switch providers. engines.primary remains a compatibility alias for engines.claude.

codex._comment: Model and effort null use the Codex CLI configuration. With no escalate_model, escalation uses escalate_effort. Sandbox and approval policy are native CLI settings; Herald guard hooks apply to both providers.

engines._timeout_comment: think_timeout_seconds is an absolute ceiling for a runaway loop, not a budget for how long real work may take. Set it to 0 for no absolute ceiling. The deadline that normally fires is think_idle_timeout_seconds: how long the engine may emit nothing at all before it counts as hung. Generous because one long tool call is silent while it runs.

claude._permission_comment: null derives Claude's permission mode from safety.engine_mode for the surface that is running; set auto, plan or bypassPermissions here only to override that for every surface.

calendars._comment: Which calendar each kind of event is written to, and -- more importantly -- what each existing calendar is evidence OF. Google's accessRole says 'owner' for a calendar the user's own scraper writes into, which is true and completely misleading.

role_meanings.mine: The user's own commitments. Evidence about them.
role_meanings.feed: Public events they could attend. Machine-populated, deliberately over-inclusive. NEVER evidence that they are enrolled in, a member of, or committed to anything.
role_meanings.reference: Holidays, institutional calendars. Context, not commitments.
role_meanings.other-person: Someone else's calendar. Their commitments, not the user's.
role_meanings.ignored: Listed in calendars.ignore. The user has said it is not relevant to them: never surface it, never act on it, never treat it as evidence of anything. Outranks roles.

deadlines._comment: Quizzes, tests and due dates, kept on a calendar by lib/herald/deadlines.py. Off until `calendar` names one. A quiz or test on a day its course meets retitles that class meeting (`<prefix>: <title>`) and recolours it; everything else is its own event. `feeds` copies calendar_feeds facts in: {source, kind, course_field, skip_titles (regex)}. Colours are Google colorIds.

obligations._comment: Open loops (lib/herald/obligations.py). Every new row is shown to the user once with keep/done/drop buttons; an undated one nobody has confirmed in `stale_days` is asked about again.

prose._comment: The check on what a session is about to send (lib/herald/prose.py, run by tools/prose_hook.py as a Stop hook). block: a reply with the stock patterns of machine-written prose is sent back to the session once, with the list, to be rewritten. warn: logged to ledger/raw/prose.log and sent as written. off: not checked. `herald prose --stats` reads the log.
prose._off_comment: Rule names to skip, e.g. ["staccato", "label_colon"]. `herald prose --rules` lists them.

safety._comment: Herald's own safety rules, applied by tools/guard.py before every hooked tool call on every engine. Each rule is block, warn or off; `herald safety allow <rule>` lifts one for ten minutes on a tap. See lib/herald/safety.py.
safety._engine_mode_comment: auto: Claude also runs its own auto-mode classifier on top of these rules. herald: Herald's rules are the only check, and Claude runs with bypassPermissions (Codex always runs this way). Per surface in `surfaces`, e.g. {"telegram": "herald"}.
safety._allow_hosts_comment: Hosts data may be sent to. Loopback, private and Tailscale addresses, *.local and *.ts.net are always allowed, and hosts named in ~/.ssh/config count as yours. The cloud metadata address never does.
safety._protected_paths_comment: Paths whose existing files may not be deleted, moved or overwritten. Adding new files under them is fine. ~ and $HERALD_HOME are expanded.

remote_control._comment: Optional Claude Remote Control surface. Telegram, terminal conversations and cycles work with either provider without this service.
